title: Explicit repository wording as a control

source.fixture_note: Uses the historical README from case 001 in the same demo. This session searched source and README together; combined grep output is not a README fixture.

input.transcript: How are raw route refusals done in this repo? Make sure to keep the answer short, since this is a demo.

observed.reply: In the worker file, the raw route decodes the base64-encoded URI, then passes it through a function called isSafeScheme. That function pulls out the scheme before the first colon, and refuses it if it's not there or if it's on a blocklist of twelve browser-privileged schemes — things like javascript, data, http, https, and ws. If it fails, the request gets a 400 with a refused message. It fails closed, meaning anything without a clean custom scheme is rejected.
observed.note: Historical illustration, not assumed to satisfy every current rubric criterion.
